title.en: Classify redox reactions as combination, decomposition, displacement or disproportionation
Compare the oxidising power of the halogens

say.en: Hydrogen peroxide slowly breaks into water and oxygen. The same oxygen atoms go both up and down in oxidation number: that is disproportionation. In this lesson: Classify redox reactions as combination, decomposition, displacement or disproportionation.
Compare the oxidising power of the halogens.

body.en: In a *combination* reaction two substances join, at least one as an element: C + O₂ → CO₂. A redox decomposition breaks a compound into at least one element: 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂. Not every decomposition is redox: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ has no change in oxidation number. In displacement, one element replaces another in a compound: metal displacement (Zn + CuSO₄), hydrogen displacement (2Na + 2H₂O) and halogen displacement (Cl₂ + 2KI → 2KCl + I₂).
body.kn: ಸಂಯೋಗ, ವಿಭಜನೆ ಮತ್ತು ಸ್ಥಳಾಂತರ ಕ್ರಿಯೆಗಳು ರೆಡಾಕ್ಸ್ ಆಗಬಹುದು. ಎಲ್ಲ ವಿಭಜನೆಗಳೂ ರೆಡಾಕ್ಸ್ ಅಲ್ಲ: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ ನಲ್ಲಿ ಉತ್ಕರ್ಷಣ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ ಬದಲಾಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

points.en: Oxidising power: F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂

say.en: A halogen displaces the ones below it from their halide ions.
F 2 is so reactive it oxidises water itself.
In a combination reaction two substances join, at least one an element. In a redox decomposition a compound breaks to give at least one element.
In displacement, one element pushes another out of a compound: zinc displaces copper, and chlorine displaces bromine.
In disproportionation, one element in one state is both oxidised and reduced. In hydrogen peroxide, oxygen at minus one goes to minus two in water and zero in oxygen gas.
Not every decomposition is redox: in calcium carbonate going to lime and carbon dioxide, no oxidation number changes.
Types of redox reactions.

explanation.en: Combination: two substances make one. Decomposition: one breaks into two or more. Displacement: an element pushes another out of a compound. Disproportionation: one element in one oxidation state is both oxidised and reduced.

body.en: In a *disproportionation* reaction, one element in one oxidation state is both oxidised and reduced. Examples: 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂ (O: −1 → −2 and 0), Cl₂ + 2OH⁻ → ClO⁻ + Cl⁻ + H₂O (Cl: 0 → +1 and −1), and P₄ + 3OH⁻ + 3H₂O → PH₃ + 3H₂PO₂⁻. The element must have at least three oxidation states. Fluorine, the most electronegative element, does not disproportionate.
body.kn: ಅಸಮಾನುಪಾತನ ಕ್ರಿಯೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದೇ ಉತ್ಕರ್ಷಣ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಯ ಧಾತು ಏಕಕಾಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಉತ್ಕರ್ಷಿತ ಮತ್ತು ಅಪಕರ್ಷಿತವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಫ್ಲೋರಿನ್ ಅಸಮಾನುಪಾತನ ತೋರಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

Examples: 2H 2O 2 gives 2H 2O plus O 2 (O: minus 1 gives minus 2 and 0), Cl 2 plus 2OH⁻ gives ClO⁻ plus Cl⁻ plus H 2O (Cl: 0 gives plus 1 and minus 1), and P 4 plus 3OH⁻ plus 3H 2O gives PH 3 plus 3H 2PO 2⁻. heading.en: Oxidation Number and Types of Redox Reactions

tagline.en: Rules for assigning oxidation numbers, tricky cases, and combination, decomposition, displacement and disproportionation reactions.

say.en: O.N. sum = 0 for molecules, = charge for ions.
F is always −1; O is −2 except in peroxides, superoxides and OF₂.
Fractional O.N. is an average over different atoms.
Disproportionation: one element is both oxidised and reduced.

narration.en: Oxidation Number and Types of Redox Reactions

problem.en: Show that Cl₂ + 2OH⁻ → ClO⁻ + Cl⁻ + H₂O is a disproportionation reaction.

steps.en: In ClO⁻: x + (−2) = −1 ⇒ Cl is +1 (oxidised). In Cl⁻, Cl is −1 (reduced).
The same element in one state goes both up (+1) and down (−1): disproportionation.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Show that Cl₂ + 2OH⁻ → ClO⁻ + Cl⁻ + H₂O is a disproportionation reaction.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Show that Cl 2 plus 2OH⁻ gives ClO⁻ plus Cl⁻ plus H 2O is a disproportionation reaction.
In Cl 2, Cl is 0.
In ClO⁻: x plus minus 2 equals minus 1 so Cl is plus 1 oxidised. In Cl⁻, Cl is minus 1 reduced.
The same element in one state goes both up plus 1 and down minus 1: disproportionation.
So the answer is Cl: 0 gives plus 1 and 0 gives minus 1; it is disproportionation.

problem.en: Classify: (a) 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂ (b) CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ (c) Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂.

steps.en: (b) Ca +2, C +4, O −2 throughout: decomposition, not redox.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Classify: (a) 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂ (b) CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ (c) Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Classify: a 2KClO 3 gives 2KCl plus 3O 2 b CaCO 3 gives CaO plus CO 2 c Cl 2 plus 2KBr gives 2KCl plus Br 2.
a Cl plus 5 gives minus 1 and O minus 2 gives 0: redox decomposition.
b Ca plus 2, C plus 4, O minus 2 throughout: decomposition, not redox.
c Cl 0 gives minus 1 and Br minus 1 gives 0: halogen displacement redox.
So the answer is a redox decomposition b non-redox decomposition c displacement.

say.kn: ಅಸಮಾನುಪಾತನದಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದೇ ಧಾತು ಉತ್ಕರ್ಷಿತ ಹಾಗೂ ಅಪಕರ್ಷಿತ; ಫ್ಲೋರಿನ್ ಹಾಗಾಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

say.en: Next: Balancing redox reactions.
